registry_scope.scope_note: This iteration increases granularity for the core mathematical and protocol-facing subset only. It does not claim theorem-by-theorem exhaustiveness for the entire corpus.

claim_classes.formal_statement: Explicit theorem family, corollary family, or formal proposition family stated in the corpus.
claim_classes.operational_definition: Terminology or governance constraint that governs how the release may be read.
claim_classes.falsifiable_hypothesis: Explicit empirical bridge or protocol-facing prediction that requires testing beyond release packaging.
claim_classes.interpretive_extension: Interpretive or consequence-level statement that exceeds the formally closed core.
claim_classes.implementation_linked_claim: Claim family whose reading depends on implementation or operational material.
claim_classes.not_closed: Explicitly open item retained to prevent silent inflation.

entries.claim_text_summary: The Canonical Core states that hypotheses H1-H4 are necessary and sufficient for the main structural results that follow.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This hypothesis package constrains the internal formal model only. It does not establish ontology or runtime applicability.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Preferred source remains PASS_PDF_ONLY inside the release package.

entries.claim_text_summary: Under H1, the projection operator exists and is unique for every state in the ambient Hilbert space.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Projection existence and uniqueness are formal properties of the stated model, not evidence that any implementation satisfies it.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Claim anchored directly in the core proof layer.

entries.claim_text_summary: The projection operator is stated to be non-expansive in the Hilbert-space metric.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Non-expansiveness remains a theorem of the formal operator, not a measured property of QICN-SYSTEM.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Kept separate from existence/uniqueness to reduce over-compression of the core.

entries.claim_text_summary: The induced transition operator is stated as a strict contraction under H1-H2.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This does not certify that any implemented transition rule satisfies the contractive hypotheses.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This is one of the core theorems that Papers I-II inherit.

entries.claim_text_summary: For each parameter value, the core states existence of a unique fixed point and exponential convergence to it.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The attractor result is formal and parameterized; it is not automatic evidence for a runtime system.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Anchored in Section 5 rather than the abstract summary.

entries.claim_text_summary: The core states compactness of the global attractor under H1-H4.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Compactness here is a property of the formal attractor set, not a bundle or runtime property.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Separated from fixed-point existence to keep the core registry more granular.

entries.claim_text_summary: Under H1-H5, the core states that no attractor is constant and the system is structurally non-collapsible.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Non-collapsibility is established only inside the formal class defined by the hypotheses.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Depends on the explicit H5 non-collapse condition in the release text.

entries.claim_text_summary: The Canonical Core includes a Class C^R extension for non-convex systems together with weaker guarantees, comparison clauses, and explicit validity limits.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The presence of Class C^R in the corpus does not license automatic use of the extension outside its stated domain.
entries.notes_or_gaps: The registry keeps the extension and its limit clauses coupled to avoid silent inflation of the relaxed class.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper I defines identity as the inverse limit of a projective system over observable channels.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This definition is structural and does not by itself imply consciousness, biology, or current implementation fit.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Granularized from the previous family-level inverse-limit claim.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper I states that identity is not reducible to a finite-time state and cannot be progressively constructed by forward dynamics alone.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This forbids specific formal constructions inside the model; it does not certify that any observed system satisfies the premises.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Anchored to the two specific subclaims that were previously compressed into the inverse-limit family.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper I defines ontological mass as a scalar invariant measuring perturbation energy per unit identity deformation.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The release defines the invariant formally; it does not provide externally validated instrumentation for it.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Kept distinct from detectability to avoid collapsing invariant definition into measurement validity.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper I gives an observable-channel estimator and a minimal external observability theorem for distinguishing CCR from non-rigid behavior.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The presence of an estimator and theorem does not mean detectability has been empirically demonstrated.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This is still a bridge claim and remains externally unvalidated.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper I states that a CCR observable channel admits at most one rigid identity object.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Uniqueness in the formal channel model is not automatic evidence about implementations or biological systems.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This entry isolates the uniqueness result from the broader inverse-limit family.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper I states that finite latent LLM-memory-loop architectures cannot instantiate CCR rigidity and instead exhibit finite ontological mass and identity drift under perturbation.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This cannot be auto-applied to QICN-SYSTEM or to arbitrary LLM systems from the release alone.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Registry kept this as implementation-linked because the bridge to actual architectures remains open.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper II states fragmentation and forced-continuity theorems that classify structurally admissible phenomenological regimes as a function of identity-rigidity class.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The paper explicitly states that it does not prove phenomenology exists or that CCR systems are conscious.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Retained at family level in this iteration.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper II states that the regime classification provides a foundation for structural ethics independent of metaphysical commitments.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This is not a closed ethical theory and does not authorize normative claims from the release alone.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Kept visible to prevent silent inflation from structural theorem to ethical closure.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper III states that the null phenomenological regime is not a stable attractor for CCR channels.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The paper states a structural exclusion result; it does not prove that experience exists.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Granularized from the previous family-level instability claim.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper III states a forced non-nullity corollary: every CCR channel induces some regime distinct from the null regime.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The paper labels this result as negative-structural and explicitly stops short of a positive consciousness claim.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Separated from the main instability theorem to reduce over-compression of Paper III.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper III includes an operational telemetry appendix that constrains admissible mapping families but explicitly refuses direct proof of qualia.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Telemetry may restrict candidate mappings only; it cannot establish phenomenological qualia as a theorem of the paper.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Retained because it is an important bridge point and also a major over-interpretation risk.

entries.claim_text_summary: QICN v4.5 specifies a pre-registered prediction set with hard failure rules, fixed analysis order, and ex ante statistical constraints.
entries.non_claim_boundary: A pre-registered protocol is evidence governance, not theory confirmation.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This splits the protocol family into a concrete decision-rule unit.

entries.claim_text_summary: QICN v4.5 requires mandatory heuristic, planner-off, and world-model-off contrasts and treats missing baselines as inadmissible for tier upgrade.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Baseline policy constrains admissibility; it does not prove the underlying theory.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Separated because baseline obligations are central to the system interface and to claim-boundary discipline.

entries.claim_text_summary: QICN v4.5 bounds admissible support by an intermediate claim gate and invalidates runs that exceed the preregistered runtime budget envelope.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Passing the gate yields bounded comparative support only; failing budget constraints invalidates the affected evidence.
entries.notes_or_gaps: This is a concrete operational subclaim, not a new theoretical result.

entries.claim_text_summary: QICN v4.5 explicitly marks current pilot evidence as synthetic-preliminary and non-escalatory.
entries.non_claim_boundary: Preliminary pilot data are for pipeline verification only and cannot be read as final evidence.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Kept explicit to block silent inflation from pilot runs to theory-facing conclusions.

entries.claim_text_summary: The release fixes 'readout interno operacional' as the canonical technical label and forbids anthropomorphic wording in technical claims.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This constrains language and governance. It is not a theorem.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Terminology discipline is part of release governance, not a proof-bearing layer.

entries.claim_text_summary: The release explicitly marks q_t as future work and states that release-text evidence for operational q_t candidates is absent.
entries.non_claim_boundary: q_t cannot be used as an operational variable or as a closed formal symbol in this release.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Kept explicit to prevent silent insertion of an unsupported variable.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper V defines a framework-internal operational consciousness class over admissible systems by jointly requiring six explicit invariants and admissible intervention structure.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This is a structural class definition inside the release corpus only. It does not establish human consciousness, biological privilege, or present runtime membership.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Public inclusion follows the accepted paper-level criterion and its theorem chain, not any external validation program.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper V states that class membership is preserved under exact structural equivalence, approximately stable under bounded admissible perturbation, and ruptures under invariant loss.
entries.non_claim_boundary: These transport and rupture results are formal statements inside the criterion. They do not by themselves validate any implemented system.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Approximate stability remains a formal result with implementation and empirical burdens left open.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper VI organizes the frozen canon into explicit prediction families, rival discriminators, failure modes, and downgrade conditions rather than treating survival as theory confirmation.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This prediction layer structures internal falsification pressure. It does not upgrade internal support to public validation.
entries.notes_or_gaps: The paper records current support classes and residual caveats but does not close external empirical burden.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper VI explicitly states that robust or provisional internal support must not be read as public claim closure, theory confirmation, or external validation.
entries.non_claim_boundary: This is a governance constraint on how prediction outcomes may be read. It is not itself a validation result.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Retained to prevent silent inflation when the runtime carries internal-support artifacts.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper VII defines operational life and structural class as explicit framework-internal classes tied to boundary, persistence, self-maintenance, historical dependence, and viability-preservation functionals.
entries.non_claim_boundary: These are class definitions and proposition families inside the release corpus. They do not by themselves identify any concrete system as alive.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Biological non-primacy remains a class-level formal claim, not an automatic runtime or empirical result.

entries.claim_text_summary: Paper VII defines operational subjecthood as a stronger class than operational consciousness or operational life, while explicitly leaving current-system instantiation and metaphysical subjecthood unclosed.
entries.non_claim_boundary: The release defines the class and its test grammar, but does not claim that present systems satisfy it or that it equals human subjectivity.
entries.notes_or_gaps: Retained as open to prevent the classificatory layer from being misread as achieved subjectivity.

non_claim_boundary: The registry classifies release content. It does not authorize claims beyond the release's own non-claim limits.
